neighbours.label: subword pieces inside Latin names and Latinate chemical names (Agricola, Agrippa, abscisic)
fire: In his short book, Tacitus praised the career of Agricola in Britain.
The governor Agricola pushed the Roman frontier deep into Caledonia.
Augustus relied on his loyal friend Agrippa to command the fleet at Actium.
The map commissioned by Agrippa was displayed in a portico in Rome.
Under drought stress the leaves accumulate abscisic acid and close their pores.
Seed dormancy is controlled largely by the hormone abscisic acid.
Historians still debate where Agricola fought the battle of Mons Graupius.
The emperor Nero was the son of Agrippina the Younger.
quiet: In his short book, Tacitus praised the career of his father-in-law in Britain.
The Roman governor pushed the frontier deep into the northern highlands.
Augustus relied on his loyal admiral to command the fleet at Actium.
The map commissioned by the emperor was displayed in a portico in Rome.
Under drought stress the leaves accumulate a hormone and close their pores.
Seed dormancy is controlled largely by temperature and moisture.
Historians still debate where the legions fought the battle in Scotland.
The emperor Nero was the son of a powerful and ambitious mother.

notes: Card: very sparse (0.011%); top examples are pieces 'icol', 'ol', 'is', 'a', 'yth' inside Agricola/Agricolae, abscisic and Agrippa.
